page: Amazon Web Services x8g.medium is a memory-optimized instance powered by the ARM-based AWS Graviton architecture with an AWS Neoverse-V2 core operating at 2.8 GHz. The instance is built on the AWS Nitro System and provisions a single dedicated physical core without hardware multithreading, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory. Cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. It operates with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions, provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include local instance storage or GPU hardware.

Benchmark results reflect the single-core configuration paired with an expansive memory-to-vCPU ratio. Single-core compute metrics fall squarely in the median range across cloud servers, scoring 1673.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1694.19 in stress-ng single-core tests. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs strongly at 14.31 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics such as stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU overall score in the bottom 10 percent due to the solitary core constraint. Memory throughput tests demonstrate 28.26 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 11.33 GB/sec for 256 MB writes, achieving an average PassMark memory score of 2137.2.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the x8g.medium offers a cost-effective entry point for deployments needing a high memory footprint without requiring parallel compute cores. Because it features a 16:1 memory-to-core ratio, it prevents the over-provisioning of CPU cores typically associated with memory-heavy platforms. Tradeoffs include low multi-core processing throughput, moderate baseline network bandwidth, and reliance entirely on remote EBS storage volumes.

The x8g.medium is suitable for small in-memory key-value caches like Redis, lightweight database nodes, background single-threaded queue consumers, and microservices requiring substantial memory capacity per thread.

Hardware acceleration covers standard AES encryption alongside 36 MB of L3 cache, with 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and no bundled local instance storage. The instance provides an efficient architectural fit for workloads that demand significant RAM capacity without the cost of unneeded CPU cores, including lightweight Redis caching instances, small relational or in-memory databases, and single-threaded batch processing services relying on network-attached storage.
